tez: Dollar General is compounding revenue in the low single digits (3.4% YoY) while expanding gross margin and growing operating income (10.8%) and net income (13.3%) faster than sales, trading at a reasonable 17.96x TTM P/E and a 7.84% parent-attributed FCF yield, with a current ratio (1.17x) and leverage profile that both compare favorably to the retail peer median (0.79x); the standalone risk to monitor is that this earnings growth has not yet translated into cash, with TTM free cash flow and operating cash flow both declining double digits year over year, a divergence that must reverse or stabilize for the thesis to hold.

tez_testleri.failure_condition: operating_cash_flow_growth remains negative below -5% in the next comparable Q1 YoY reading
net_profit_growth falls below 5% year over year

belirleyici_veriler.aciklama: P/E of 17.96x on TTM parent net income is a moderate valuation for a retailer showing double-digit earnings growth.
Current ratio of 1.17x compares favorably against the 5-peer retail median of 0.79x.
Consolidated net income grew 13.3% year over year (444.1 versus 391.9 million USD), a favorable threshold result.
TTM free cash flow declined 34.4% year over year (364.6 versus 556.2 million USD in the comparable YTD), an adverse threshold result.
Piotroski F-Score is 7/9, failing only on 'Improving current ratio' and 'No increase in shares outstanding', otherwise passing all profitability and leverage components.

tezi_bozacak_kosullar: Operating cash flow and free cash flow continue to decline year over year in subsequent quarters instead of stabilizing, indicating the earnings-to-cash divergence is structural rather than a capex/working-capital timing effect.
Net income or operating income growth decelerates materially or reverses, removing the earnings-quality justification for the current P/E multiple.
Current ratio deteriorates below 1.0, eroding the liquidity advantage versus peers.
Share count begins increasing meaningfully, diluting the improving per-share earnings trend the Piotroski score otherwise supports.
belirsizlik: No structured long-term debt or lease maturity schedule was extracted, limiting assessment of refinancing risk timing.
Issuer-reported EBITDA and net-debt APM are not disclosed, so EV/EBITDA could not be calculated.
Cash paid for share repurchases during 2025-FY is not available, leaving total capital-return magnitude (beyond dividends) unclear.
Whether the FCF/OCF decline is driven by one-off capex timing or working-capital shifts versus a structural trend cannot be determined from a single quarter of YTD data.
